Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the time on Monday. As discussed, I've put together a renewal proposal that aligns with Acme's forecasting for H1 — primary ask is to add an additional reserved pool (16A GPUs) that sits beside your existing 32A pool. The main points in this draft: 

- Reserved pool: +16 A100s (reserved capacity) for predictable throughput during daytime peaks.
- Throughput SLA: 99.5% of requests under 250ms p50 and p95 under our current model profile.
- Overflow policy: two-tier approach (soft cap with credit-backed burst + optional on-demand behind soft cap).
- Pricing: blended rate for reserved units, overage pricing only applies after reserved credits are consumed.

I'm attaching the proposal and an annotated SLA diff. Key question for you: would you prefer a hard cap (no on-demand spill) or to allow on-demand overflow at a higher per-token rate? The hybrid we suggested keeps production stable while avoiding silent throttles.

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 11:04 AM Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@acme-robotics.com> wrote:
> Can Ben or Aditya weigh in on the technical behavior for the soft cap?

Short answer: the soft cap is elastic but controlled. Proposal we typically recommend: 

- Soft cap window: a short-term headroom (e.g., 20-30% above reserved capacity) that consumes burst credits at request time. Bursts are rate-limited per second to avoid noisy-neighbor spikes.
- Credit accounting: you pre-purchase burst credits as part of the renewal; credits are consumed first, then on-demand pricing applies.
- Fallbacks: configurable policy — prefer model-variant fallback (lower-cost / lower-latency variant) OR graceful degradation (queued requests with retry-after), OR immediate shift to on-demand with higher price.
- Throttling behavior: deterministic token-level pacing rather than opaque drops; requests above threshold return 429 with Retry-After unless on-demand is enabled.

Aditya — can you add a short cost delta example for 2x peak across a 24-hour window for the proposal? I'll draft language for the support-side runbook so Acme's SRE knows what to expect.

- Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi team / Samantha — adding the cost sketch Ben requested below (high level):

Scenario assumptions:
- Baseline reserved capacity: 32A + new 16A reserved = 48A total reserved
- Typical daily demand: 10M tokens/day; peak-event demand: 20M tokens/day (2x) for 6 peak hours
- Burst window headroom: 25% of reserved pool before credits consumed

Estimated monthly impact (rounded):
- Reserved incremental monthly seat cost (16A): $36,000 (committed rate)
- If using burst credits only (pre-purchased 200M token credits): additional ~$3,200/month amortized
- If allowing on-demand overflow for the 2x peak (worst-case capture ~120M tokens of overflow): ~ $18,000 in overage (on-demand rate)

Net: Hybrid with prepaid burst credits caps the expected overage to low thousands/mo; fully open on-demand covers unplanned surges but may add mid-five-figure risk in extreme months.

Operational notes: no VPC changes required for the reserved pool attach; if you enable on-demand fallback to a hosted variant we will route through existing secure connectivity — we will coordinate a brief maintenance window to validate egress/firewall rules but nothing heavy.

Samantha — happy to produce a 95th-percentile cost estimate with your historical 90-day usage if you can share the token/time histogram.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

3) SLA amendment: add throughput guarantees for the reserved pool (we'll attach the SLA diff).
4) Mid-term expansion: yes — you can add reserved GPUs mid-term at pro-rated pricing; contract clause added to the attached doc to make this operationally simple (Proc signs a PO, we provision within 7 business days).
